inputs.label: Desired AUC
help: Desired AUC must be between 1.5 and 7.5.

inputs.label: GFR equation
help: Used only when GFR is not known. Jelliffe reports mL/min/1.73m².

steps.expr: calvert_gfr if (gfr_known == 'Yes') else (min((((0.85 if gfr_sex == 0 else 1) * ((140 - gfr_age) / (gfr_srcr)) * (gfr_weight / 72)) if (gfr_equation == 'Cockcroft-Gault') else ((0.9 if gfr_sex == 0 else 1) * (98 - (0.8 * (gfr_age - 20))) / gfr_srcr)), max_cr_cl_input) if (max_cr_cl_input > 0) else (((0.85 if gfr_sex == 0 else 1) * ((140 - gfr_age) / (gfr_srcr)) * (gfr_weight / 72)) if (gfr_equation == 'Cockcroft-Gault') else ((0.9 if gfr_sex == 0 else 1) * (98 - (0.8 * (gfr_age - 20))) / gfr_srcr)))

content.equation:
Carboplatin Dosage:
Carboplatin Dosage = Desired AUC * (GFR + 25)
• Carboplatin Dosage is calculated in mg
• Desired AUC is input in mg/mL*min
• GFR is input in mL/min
o If GFR Known is "No", GFR is calculated as described
Glomerular Filtration Rate (GFR):
Dosing recommendations in the manufacturer's labeling are based on an actual glomerular
filtration rate (GFR) measurement. However, in clinical practice, the Cockcroft-Gault
formula is frequently used to estimate GFR. The Jelliffe formula is also commonly
used; however, both methods can underestimate or overestimate the GFR and result in
under- or overdosing carboplatin. When calculating the carboplatin dose using the
Calvert formula and an estimated GFR, the laboratory method used to measure serum
creatinine may impact dosing. Compared to other methods used, standardized Isotope
Dilution Mass Spectrometry (IDMS) may underestimate serum creatinine values in
patients with low creatinine values (eg, ≤0.7 mg/dL) and may overestimate GFR in
patients with normal renal function. This could result in higher calculated carboplatin
doses and increased toxicities. If using IDMS, the Food and Drug Administration
(FDA) recommends that clinicians considering capping estimated GFRs at a
maximum of 125 mL/min to avoid potential toxicity.
Note: In most situations, the use of the patient's ideal body weight (IBW) is recommended
for estimating renal function, except when the patient's actual body weight (ABW) is
less than ideal. Use of actual body weight (ABW) in obese patients (and possibly
patients with ascites) may significantly overestimate renal function. Some clinicians
prefer to use an adjusted body weight in such cases [eg, IBW + 0.4 (ABW - IBW)]; the
adjustment factor may vary based on practitioner and/or institutional preference.
Cockcroft-Gault Method:
Males: CrCl = [(140 - Age) * Weight] / (72 * Creatinine)
Females: CrCl = {[(140 - Age) * Weight] / (72 * Creatinine)} * 0.85
• CrCl = creatinine clearance; calculated in mL/minute
• Age is input in years
• Weight is input in kg
• Creatinine is input in mg/dL
Jelliffe Method:
Males: CrCl = {98 - [0.8 * (Age - 20)]} / (Creatinine)
Females: CrCl = {[(98 - [0.8 * (Age - 20)] / (Creatinine)} * 0.9
• CrCl = creatinine clearance; calculated in mL/minute/1.73 m2
• Age is input in years
• Creatinine is input in mg/dL
content.data_input_disclaimer: ONLY DIGITS 0 TO 9 AND A SINGLE DECIMAL POINT "." ARE ACCEPTABLE AS NUMERIC INPUTS. ATTEMPTED INPUT OF OTHER CHARACTERS INTO A NUMERIC FIELD MAY LEAD TO AN INCORRECT RESULT.
content.instructions: To perform a calculation, enter the required variables. Once all the inputs are entered, click the "Calculate" button to perform the calculation. Any time an input variable is adjusted, the "Calculate" button must be clicked to populate the new output. To start over, click the "Reset" button to clear all values and begin the calculation again. The target AUC usually ranges from 1.5 to 7.5 mg/mL x minutes, with 5 to 7.5 being the most common. An AUC of 2 is used primarily in weekly dosing and an AUC of 4 is used frequently in elderly patients. Higher target AUCs can lead to toxicity, specifically thrombocytopenia and neutropenia.

conflicts.detail: when GFR is not known it is estimated with the Cockcroft-Gault or Jelliffe equation taken from this corpus's own calculators, because the shared library the PDF calls is not in the PDF; confirm against the live app before relying on it
